title: Cheapest Way to Multiply a Chain
statement:
You must multiply a chain of `n` matrices in the given order. Matrix `i` has `d_{i-1}` rows and `d_i` columns. Multiplying a matrix of size `a x b` by one of size `b x c` costs `a * b * c` and gives a matrix of size `a x c`. Matrix multiplication is associative, so you may choose the order (the brackets) freely.

Find the smallest total cost to multiply the whole chain. A chain of one matrix costs `0`.

## Input
The first line contains `n`. The second line contains `d_0 ... d_n`.

## Output
Print the smallest total cost.

## Constraints
- `1 <= n <= 90`
- `1 <= d_i <= 100`
